name: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
dates: Year round, Pinnacle Road weather dependent
unique: The pass through the Cumberland escarpment that Boone's Wilderness Road crossed, where the borders of Kentucky, Virginia and Tennessee meet, with a four mile ridge trail and an overlook that shows all three states at once.
buzz: The Pinnacle Overlook is the payoff and the walk along the ridge to the gap is better than the drive. Rangers lead walks through the old iron furnace and the cave.

name: Gap Cave Tours
unique: A ranger led walk into a cave that soldiers, travelers and saltpeter miners used for two centuries, with stalactites, underground streams and the signatures of Civil War soldiers still on the walls.
buzz: The tour is small and books out in summer. Guides point out the 1800s graffiti, which is the part people talk about afterward.

name: Tazewell Courthouse Square
unique: A courthouse square in the valley below the gap, in a county that was the gateway for everyone crossing into Kentucky before the railroads made the pass irrelevant.
buzz: A ten minute stop on the way to the park. The old commercial block is intact and the town is honest about being a pass through place.

name: Brushy Mountain State Penitentiary
customer: Dark tourism people, families with teens, history buffs
unique: A closed maximum security prison in a hollow under Frozen Head, open for self guided tours through cell blocks, the death chamber and the yard, with recordings by the guards and inmates who worked there.
buzz: The audio tour is the reason it works, and former staff are often on site to answer questions. James Earl Ray escaped from here, and the tour does not dodge the hard parts.

name: Obed Wild and Scenic River
dates: Year round, water levels decide paddling
unique: A national wild and scenic river with class three and four whitewater, sandstone cliffs bolted for climbing, and a gorge trail system that sees almost no one outside local paddlers.
buzz: Paddlers watch the gauge and go when it rains. The climbing at Lilly Bluff is well known in the southeast and the hiking is empty in every season.

name: Frozen Head State Park
unique: More than thirteen thousand acres of steep Cumberland Mountain terrain with one of the largest stands of virgin timber in the state and a spring wildflower show that draws botanists from across the region.
buzz: The hike to the fire tower is the local test piece and the trillium in April is the reason naturalists come. Some facilities have been closed for renovation, so check before you go.

name: Wartburg Courthouse Square
unique: A small German settled county seat on the plateau with a courthouse and a block of storefronts, sitting between the prison tour and the river gorge.
buzz: Ten minutes and a good sandwich. The town exists because of coal and timber and it does not pretend otherwise.

name: Norris Lake
dates: Year round, peak May to September
unique: Thirty four thousand acres of deep clear water in the Cumberland Mountains with eight hundred miles of shoreline, twenty two marinas and floating cabins, built as a TVA project in the 1930s.
buzz: The water clarity is the selling point and the shoreline is steep enough that the lake stays quiet. Houseboat weeks book a year out.

name: Cove Lake State Park
unique: A small park on a quiet arm of Norris Lake with a campground, a paved trail around the cove and a swimming area, right off Interstate 75.
buzz: The easy stop for a lake afternoon on a road trip. Campers rate the sites for shade and water access.

name: Cumberland Trail State Park
unique: Tennessee's first linear state park, a three hundred mile trail along the Cumberland escarpment that is being built segment by segment, with some of the steepest and most exposed walking in the state.
buzz: Section hikers treat it as a long term project. The segments near LaFollette have overlooks and rock formations without the crowds of the Smokies.

name: LaFollette Downtown
unique: A coal and railroad town laid out in the 1890s with a long commercial block, now the supply stop for the lake and the trail country around it.
buzz: Not restored and not trying to be. Useful, cheap and close to the water.

name: Brimstone Recreation
customer: ATV and side by side riders, families, groups
unique: Nearly twenty thousand acres of privately managed off road trail in the Cumberland Mountains, with cabin rentals, a general store and trail that runs to the top of the plateau.
buzz: Riders come from several states with trailers and stay the weekend. The trails are maintained and the mud is the point.

name: North Cumberland Wildlife Management Area
unique: A hundred and forty thousand acres of reclaimed coal country on the Cumberland Mountains where elk were reintroduced, with viewing areas, gated trails and almost no facilities.
buzz: Elk sightings are common at dawn in the grass flats. Hunters draw tags for a limited season and everyone else comes for the quiet.

name: Oneida and the Big South Fork Gateway
unique: The Tennessee entrance town for the Big South Fork, with an outfitter row, a rail trail and a downtown that runs on riders, paddlers and hunters rather than tourists.
buzz: Practical rather than pretty. The trailhead and the gear shops are the reason to stop.

name: Huntsville Courthouse Square
unique: A small courthouse square in the county seat, a few miles from the off road park and the Big South Fork, in country that was logged and mined and is now mostly public land.
buzz: A supply stop with a diner and a hardware store. Nothing to plan a trip around and useful when you are here.

name: Bush's Beans Visitor Center
unique: A twelve thousand square foot visitor center beside the plant that cans the beans, with a turn of the century general store, the company story and the secret family recipe told as a piece of east Tennessee history.
buzz: Free, air conditioned and better than a corporate lobby. The general store and the bean displays keep kids busy for an hour.

name: Historic Dandridge
unique: The second oldest town in Tennessee, laid out in 1792 on a grid of brick and frame buildings above Douglas Lake, with a self guided walking tour and a courthouse that has been in use for two centuries.
buzz: The walking tour is short, free and genuinely old. The town flooded partially when the lake was built, and the dike that protects it is a local landmark.

name: Douglas Lake
unique: Thirty thousand acres of TVA water against the Smoky Mountains with a national reputation for largemouth bass, thirty plus marinas and public access areas along the Jefferson County shore.
buzz: Bass anglers rate it among the best in the country and the mountain backdrop makes it the postcard lake of east Tennessee.

name: Cherokee Lake
unique: A TVA reservoir with a reputation for crappie and striped bass, and a shoreline of coves and islands that stays quieter than Douglas next door.
buzz: Crappie fishermen in spring fill the coves. The lake is a locals' lake rather than a resort one.

name: Music on the Town in Dandridge
unique: Free outdoor concerts behind town hall on Thursday nights in September, with lawn chairs, local food and the courthouse square as a backdrop.
buzz: Small, free and exactly the kind of thing that makes a town worth living in. Bring a chair.

name: Pigeon River Whitewater Rafting
dates: April to October, dam release schedule
unique: Rafting on a river that runs off a controlled dam release through the Cherokee National Forest gorge, with a upper section of class three and four rapids and a lower section easy enough for children.
buzz: Outfitters run trips all day in summer and the water is cold even in August. It is the closest big whitewater to Gatlinburg and Pigeon Forge.

name: Five Rivers Adventures
unique: A base camp on Dorsey Road in Cosby running raft trips, ziplines and a ropes course from one parking lot, on the quiet side of the Smokies.
buzz: Reviews single out the guides with kids and the fact that you can do two activities in a day without moving the car.

name: Cherokee National Forest around Cosby
unique: The Tennessee side of the national forest that wraps the Smokies, with trails from Cosby into the park, trout streams, and campgrounds that stay empty compared with the Gatlinburg side.
buzz: Locals hike here to avoid the park traffic. The Cosby campground and the Gabes Mountain trail are the quiet alternative.

name: Newport Downtown
unique: The county seat for the Pigeon River gorge, with a courthouse square, a farmers market and the outfitters and diners that serve the rafting trade.
buzz: A practical stop on the way to the river. The square has recovered from the flood years and the food is cheap.
